{3} He informs that He {created the heavens and the earth in truth}, so that the servants may take them as evidence of the greatness of their Creator and of the attributes of perfection that belong to Him, and so that they may know that He created them as a dwelling for His servants, who worship Him by what He commands them through the laws (shara'i') that He sent down upon the tongues of His messengers. {4} When He mentioned the creation of the heavens [and the earth], He mentioned the creation of what is in them, and He began with the most noble of it, which is man, saying: {He created man from a drop (nutfah)}: He ceaselessly manages it, nurtures it and causes it to grow until it becomes a complete human being with all its outward and inward organs perfect, having been overwhelmed by His abundant blessings. When he is complete, he boasts of himself and becomes self-admiring. {Then he is an open adversary}: It may be that the meaning is: then he is an adversary to his Lord; he disbelieves in Him, disputes with His messengers, denies His signs, and forgets his original creation and the blessings God bestowed upon him, and so he uses them to aid his disobedience.
It may also be that the meaning is that God originated the human from a drop, then never ceased to move him from one stage to another until he became rational, articulate, possessing intellect and opinion, disputing and arguing; so let the servant thank his Lord who brought him to this state, a state over which he has no power to exercise any of it.

{5} {And the cattle He created for you}: that is, for your sake and for your benefit and welfare. Among their great benefits is that {for you in them is warmth}, through what you make from their wool, hair, fur and hides: clothing, rugs and tents. {And} for you in them are {benefits} other than that, {and from them you eat}.

{6} {And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home at evening and when you send them out to pasture}: that is, at the time of their returning and resting and calm, and the time of their movement and grazing. This is because none of their beauty returns to them; rather, it is you who adorn yourselves with them, just as you adorn yourselves with your clothing, your children and your wealth, and take pride in that.

{7} {And they carry your loads}: heavy burdens, and indeed they carry you {to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship (shiqq al-anfus)}: but God subjected them to you; some of them you ride, and some of them you load with whatever you wish of burdens, to distant lands and far-flung regions. {Indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful}: since He has made subject to you what you are compelled to and need. So to Him belongs praise, as befits the majesty of His Face, the greatness of His dominion, and the vastness of His generosity and kindness.

{8} {And horses, mules and donkeys}: We made them subject to you, {that you may ride them and as adornment}: that is, at times you use them out of necessity for riding, and at times for beauty and adornment. As for what has no counterpart, if it were mentioned they would not recognize it nor understand its meaning. Instead, He mentions a comprehensive principle that includes what they know and what they do not know, just as He described the bliss of Paradise: He named what we know and witness a counterpart of, such as the date palm, grapes and pomegranates, and summarized what we have no counterpart for in His saying: {In both of them are two kinds of every fruit}. As for the crooked path in beliefs and deeds, which is everything that opposes the straight path, it cuts one off from God and leads to the abode of misery. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 24–29:

{24} Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the intensity of the polytheists' denial of Allah's signs: {And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?"} That is: when they are asked about the Qur'an and the revelation, which is the greatest blessing Allah has bestowed upon the servants, what is your statement about it? Do you thank Allah for this blessing and acknowledge it, or do you disbelieve and obstinately oppose it? So their answer is the most loathsome and ugly of answers. They say about it that it is {tales of the ancients}; that is, a lie which Muhammad invented against Allah, and it is nothing but the stories of the earlier people which people have passed down from generation to generation, some of them true and some of them false.

{25} They uttered this statement, called their followers to it, and bore their own burden and the burden of those who followed them until the Day of Resurrection. As for His saying {and [they bear] the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge}: that is, the burdens of the blind followers who have no knowledge except what they were called to, so they bear the sin of what they were called to. As for those who have knowledge, each one bears his own crime, because he knew what they knew. {Unquestionably, evil is what they bear!} That is: wretched is what they have taken on of a burden that weighs down their backs, from their own burden and the burden of those whom they led astray.

{26–27} {Those before them did plot,} against their messengers, and they devised all kinds of stratagems to reject what the messengers brought them, and they built from their plotting great, towering palaces. {So Allah came at their structure from its foundations;} that is, the command came to them from its base and foundation. {The roof fell on them from above them,} so what they had built became a punishment with which they were punished. {And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.} This was because they thought that this structure would benefit them and protect them from punishment, but their punishment came through what they had built and established. This is among the finest examples of Allah's nullification of the plotting of His enemies. They reflected and calculated concerning what the messengers brought, and when they denied it, they made for themselves foundations and bases of falsehood to which they returned and by which they repulsed what the messengers brought. They also devised stratagems to inflict harm and injury upon the messengers and those who followed them, so their plotting became a calamity upon them, and their scheming became their own destruction. That is because their plotting is evil, and {evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own people.} This is in the world; the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful. For this reason He said: {Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them;} that is, He will expose them before all creation and make clear to them their lying and their fabrication against Allah. {And He will say, "Where are My partners, for whose sake you used to oppose [Me]?"} That is: you used to fight and oppose Allah and His party for their sake, claiming that they are partners with Allah. When He asks them this question, they will have no answer except to admit their misguidance and acknowledge their obstinacy. They will say: {They have departed from us,} {and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.} {Those who were given knowledge will say,} that is: the scholars who are devoted to their Lord: {"Indeed, disgrace this Day and evil are upon the disbelievers"} that is, on the Day of Resurrection, [{and evil}, that is,] the punishment, {upon the disbelievers.} In this is the virtue of the people of knowledge, that they are the ones who speak the truth in this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand, and that their words carry weight with Allah and with His creation.

{28} Then He mentions what will be done to them at death and on the Day of Resurrection, saying: {those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves;} that is, they are taken in this state in which their wrongdoing and error have multiplied, and it is known what the wrongdoers encounter in that station of various kinds of punishment, disgrace, and humiliation. {Then they will offer submission,} that is: they will submit and deny what they used to worship besides Allah, and they will say: {"We did not used to do any evil."} It will be said to them: {"Yes! Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do."} So denial will benefit you nothing. This occurs at some of the stations of the Resurrection: they deny what they were upon in the world, thinking that this will benefit them; but when their own bodily parts testify against them and what they were upon becomes clear, they acknowledge and confess. For this reason they do not enter the Fire until they confess their sins.

{29} When they enter the gates of Hell, each people of deeds enter through the gate suited to their condition. {Wretched is the abode of the arrogant:} the Fire of Hell, for it is the abode of regret and remorse, the dwelling place of misery and pain, the place of sorrows and griefs, and the position of the wrath of the Living, the Self-Subsisting. Its punishment is not lightened for them, nor is its painful torment lifted from them for a single day. The Lord, the Most Merciful, has turned away from them, and has made them taste the mighty punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verse 35:

{35} That is: the polytheists argued for their polytheism by the will of Allah, saying that if Allah had willed, they would not have associated partners with Him, nor would they have forbidden any of the cattle that He made lawful, such as the baheera (a she-camel whose ears were slit and released), the wasila (a ewe that gave birth to a female followed by a male, and was then left unslaughtered), the haam (a stallion camel left to roam freely), and the like, besides Him. This is a false argument, for if it were true, Allah would not have punished those before them who associated others with Him; rather, He punished them with the most severe punishment. Had He loved this from them, He would not have punished them. Their purpose in this was nothing but to reject the truth brought by the messengers. Otherwise, they have knowledge that they have no proof against Allah, for Allah commanded them and forbade them, empowered them to carry out what He imposed upon them, and gave them strength and a will from which their actions proceed. Therefore, their argument from divine decree and predestination is among the most false of falsehoods. Moreover, everyone knows through their senses the human capacity to perform every act they wish without anyone opposing them. Thus they combined the denial of Allah, the denial of His messengers, and the denial of rational and sensory matters.

{So is there upon the messengers except the clear conveyance?} That is: the clear, evident message that reaches the hearts, leaving no proof for anyone against Allah. When the messengers have conveyed to them the command and prohibition of their Lord, and they argue against them by predestination, then the messengers have no part in the matter; their reckoning rests only with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

{36} He, may He be exalted, informs that His proof has been established upon all nations, and that there is no nation, past or later, except that God has sent to it a messenger, and they all agree upon one call and one religion, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner. {That worship God and avoid the Taghut (false deities/transgressors)}. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verse 43–44:

{43} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {We sent not before you except men} (i.e., you are not an innovation among the messengers; We did not send before you angels, but rather perfect men, not women). {To whom We revealed} (of the laws and rulings, which are of His grace and benevolence toward His servants, without them bringing anything from themselves). {So ask the people of the Reminder} (i.e., the previous scriptures), {if you do not know} (the news of the former peoples, and you doubt whether Allah sent men). So ask those who have knowledge of that, those to whom the Zubur (scriptures) and the clear proofs (al-bayyinat) were sent down, who learned them and understood them; for all of them have established among themselves that Allah sent none but men, to whom He revealed, from among the people of the towns.

The generality of this verse includes praise of the people of knowledge, and that the highest type of knowledge is knowledge of the revealed Book of Allah. For Allah commanded those who do not know to refer to them in all matters. Implicit in this is a certification (ta'dil) of the people of knowledge and a commendation of them, since He commanded that they be asked, and that by this the ignorant person is freed from responsibility. This indicates that Allah entrusted them with His revelation and its sending down, and that they are commanded to purify themselves and to adorn themselves with the attributes of perfection.

{44} The best of the people of the Reminder are the people of this magnificent Qur'an, for they are truly the people of the Reminder, and more deserving than others of this name. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 48–50:

{48} He, exalted is He, says: {Have they not considered} (i.e., the doubters concerning the Oneness of their Lord, His greatness and His perfection) {at what Allah has created of things} (i.e., all of His creation), and how their shadows incline {from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah} (i.e., all of them prostrate to their Lord, submissive to His greatness and majesty), {while they are humbled} (i.e., abased under subjugation, governance and dominion); there is none of them except that its forelock is in the hand of Allah, and its management is with Him.

{49} {And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures} (among the rational and the non-rational animals), {and the angels} (the noble ones). He singled them out after the generality because of their excellence, their nobility and the abundance of their worship; for this reason He said: {and they are not arrogant} (i.e., from worshipping Him), despite their number, the greatness of their characters and their strength; as Allah, the Exalted, said: {The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]}.

{50} {They fear their Lord above them} (when He praised them for their abundant obedience and submission to Allah, He praised them for fearing Allah, who is above them in essence, dominion and the perfection of His attributes; so they are humbled under His dominion). {And they do what they are commanded} (i.e., whatever Allah, the Exalted, commands them, they comply with His command willingly and by choice). The prostration of creatures to Allah, the Exalted, is of two kinds: prostration of compulsion and of indication of the attributes of perfection that He possesses, and this is general to every creature, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked, rational animal and others. And prostration of choice, which is specific to His friends and the believing servants, among the angels and other creatures.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 56–60:

{56} God informs us of the ignorance and injustice of the polytheists, and of their fabricating lies against God. They assign to their idols, which neither know nor benefit nor harm, a portion of what God has provided and bestowed upon them. Thus they use His provision to aid them in associating others with Him, and they draw near to carved idols by means of it, as God the Exalted says: ﴿And they assign to God a portion of what He has created of the crops and cattle, and they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach God...﴾ [6:136], to the end of the verse. ﴿By God, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ It is said (to them): ﴿Did God permit you this, or do you invent lies against God?﴾ [10:59]. And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God on the Day of Resurrection? He will punish them for that with the most severe punishment.

{57–59} ﴿And they assign to God daughters﴾: they said that the angels, the honored servants, are the daughters of God. ﴿And for themselves what they desire﴾; that is, they assign to themselves males, to the extent that they hate daughters with intense hatred. So one of them, ﴿when he is given news of a female, his face becomes dark﴾: from the grief that has befallen him, ﴿and he is filled with suppressed rage﴾; that is, he suppresses grief and sorrow when he is given news of a female. He is even humiliated among his own kind, and hides himself from them because of the evil of what he has been given news of. Then he applies his corrupt mind and opinion to what he will do with that girl of whom he has been given news: ﴿Will he keep her despite contempt, or bury her in the dust?﴾; that is, will he leave her alive without killing her, in humiliation and disgrace, or will he bury her alive? This is the burying of infants by which God censured the polytheists. ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.﴾ For they described God with what does not befit His majesty, by attributing offspring to Him. Then this was not enough for them, until they attributed to Him the worse of the two divisions, namely females, whom they themselves disdain and hate. So how could they attribute them to God the Exalted? Evil is the judgment they make.

{60} Since this is among the evil similitudes that His enemies, the polytheists, attributed to Him, God the Exalted said: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil﴾; that is, the deficient similitude and the complete defect. ﴿And to God belongs the highest attribute﴾: and it is every attribute of perfection, and every perfection in existence, for God is most worthy of it, without this necessarily implying any deficiency in any way. And He has the highest attribute in the hearts of His friends, which is glorification, reverence, love, turning to Him in repentance, and knowledge. ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might﴾: who has subjugated all things, and all created beings have submitted to Him entirely. ﴿the Wise﴾: who places things in their proper places, so He does not command nor act except in ways that are worthy of praise, and His perfection in that is praised.

{70} He, exalted is He, informs that He is the One who created the servants and moved them through creation stage by stage, and then, after they complete their terms, He takes them in death. Among them is one whom He lets live until he is returned to "the most decrepit age" (ilā arḏal al-ʿumur), that is, the lowest and most degraded age, at which a person reaches the weakening of his outward and inward powers. Even the intellect, which is the essence of a human being, grows weaker, to the point that he forgets what he used to know and his mind becomes like the mind of a child. This is why He said: ﴿So that he knows nothing after having known. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Powerful.﴾ That is, His knowledge and power encompass all things, and among that is what He moves the human being through in stages of creation, one creation after another, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Powerful.﴾

This is one of the proofs of His Oneness and of the ugliness of associating partners with Him. He, exalted is He, says: just as you share in being created and provided for, yet Allah {has preferred some of you over others in provision}. So He made some of you free, who have wealth and property, and made some of you slaves, who own nothing of the world. Just as their masters, whom Allah has preferred over them in provision, do not {give their provision to what their right hands possess, so that they are equal in it}, and they regard this as something impossible, so likewise are those you associate with Allah: they are slaves who have not the least particle of dominion. So how do you make them partners with Allah, exalted is He? Is this not among the greatest injustice and ingratitude for the blessings of Allah? For this reason He said: {Then do they deny the blessing of Allah?} If they acknowledged the blessing and attributed it to the One who bestowed it, they would not have associated anyone with Him.

{72} He, may He be exalted, informs of His great favour upon His servants: He made for them spouses (azwaj) so that they might find tranquillity in them, and He made for them, from their spouses, children who gladden their eyes, serve them, fulfil their needs, and benefit them in many ways. He also provided them with good things (al-tayyibat), of food and drink and apparent blessings, which the servants cannot count. ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ That is: Do they believe in falsehood, which was not a thing worth mentioning, and then Allah brought it into existence, while it has nothing of its existence except nonexistence? It does not create, provide, or manage any affair whatsoever. This applies generally to everything that is worshipped besides Allah, for it is false; so how do the polytheists take them as gods besides Allah? ﴿And in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve﴾: they deny it, and they use it to aid them in disobeying Allah and disbelieving in Him. Is this not among the greatest of injustices, the most profligate of immoralities, and the most foolish of follies?!

{73–74} He, exalted is He, informs of the ignorance and wrongdoing of the polytheists, that they worship, besides Him, deities which they have taken as partners to God, while they do not possess for them any provision from the heavens and the earth. They do not send down rain or sustenance, nor do they cause anything of the plants of the earth to grow, nor do they own an atom's weight in the heavens and the earth, nor are they able even if they wished. For one who does not own a thing may sometimes have strength and capability to benefit one who is connected to him, but these do not own and do not have power. This is the attribute of their deities. How then did they make them equal with God and liken them to the Owner of the earth and the heavens, to whom belongs all dominion, all praise and all strength? For this reason He said: ﴿So do not strike forth examples for God﴾, which imply equating Him with His creation. ﴿Indeed, God knows, and you do not know﴾. So it is incumbent upon us not to speak about Him without knowledge, and to listen to the examples the All-Knowing has struck. Therefore, exalted is He, struck two examples, for Himself and for those who are worshipped besides Him:

{75} The first: a slave under ownership, i.e., a bondman who does not own himself and possesses nothing of wealth or worldly goods. The second: a free man, wealthy, whom God has granted a good provision of all kinds of wealth, and who is generous and loves to do good; so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are these two equal? They are not equal. Yet they are both created, and their equality is not impossible. If the two are not equal, then how could the created slave, who has no ownership, no power and no ability, but is rather poor in every respect, be equal to the Lord, the Creator, the Owner of all kingdoms, who is capable of everything? For this reason He praised Himself and specified Himself with praise in all its kinds, saying: ﴿All praise is due to God﴾. It is as if it were said: if the matter is so, why did the polytheists equate their deities with God? He said: ﴿Rather, most of them do not know﴾. Had they known the reality of knowledge, they would not have dared to commit the great shirk.

{76} The second example is that of ﴿two men, one of them mute﴾, who neither hears nor speaks, and ﴿who has no power over anything﴾, neither little nor much, ﴿and is a burden upon his master﴾, i.e., his master must serve him, and he is unable to serve himself. He is deficient in every respect. Are these two equal, the one who ﴿enjoins justice, and is on a straight path﴾? His words are just and his actions are upright. Just as the two are not equal, so one who is worshipped besides God, who cannot take care of any of His own affairs, is not equal to one who speaks only truth and does only what is praiseworthy. Had God not sustained these affairs, he would not be able to do anything of them. He cannot be a peer or rival to the One who says only the truth and does only what deserves praise.

Therefore, exalted is He, struck two examples, for Himself and for those who are worshipped besides Him:

{75} The first: a slave under ownership, i.e., a bondman who does not own himself and possesses nothing of wealth or worldly goods. The second: a free man, wealthy, whom God has granted a good provision of all kinds of wealth, and who is generous and loves to do good; so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are these two equal? They are not equal. Yet they are both created, and their equality is not impossible. If the two are not equal, then how could the created slave, who has no ownership, no power and no ability, but is rather poor in every respect, be equal to the Lord, the Creator, the Owner of all kingdoms, who is capable of everything? For this reason He praised Himself and specified Himself with praise in all its kinds, saying: ﴿All praise is due to God﴾. It is as if it were said: if the matter is so, why did the polytheists equate their deities with God? He said: ﴿Rather, most of them do not know﴾. Had they known the reality of knowledge, they would not have dared to commit the great shirk.

{76} The second example is that of ﴿two men, one of them mute﴾, who neither hears nor speaks, and ﴿who has no power over anything﴾, neither little nor much, ﴿and is a burden upon his master﴾, i.e., his master must serve him, and he is unable to serve himself. He is deficient in every respect. Are these two equal, the one who ﴿enjoins justice, and is on a straight path﴾? His words are just and his actions are upright. Just as the two are not equal, so one who is worshipped besides God, who cannot take care of any of His own affairs, is not equal to one who speaks only truth and does only what is praiseworthy. Had God not sustained these affairs, he would not be able to do anything of them. He cannot be a peer or rival to the One who says only the truth and does only what deserves praise.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verse 77:

{77} That is: He, exalted is He, is the One who alone has the unseen of the heavens and the earth. None knows the hidden things, the inner states, and the secrets except Him. Among these is the knowledge of the Hour (al-Sa'ah). No one knows when it will come except Allah. When it comes and becomes manifest, it will not be except ﴿like the blink of an eye, or even closer﴾ with respect to that. Then people will rise from their graves until the Day of their resurrection and their gathering, and opportunities will be lost for those who wish for respite. ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾: so the resurrection of the dead should not be considered strange given His all-encompassing power.

{78} That is: He alone is the One who bestows these blessings, when {He brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing}, and unable to do anything. Then {He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts}. He singled out these three organs for their nobility and excellence, and because they are the key to every kind of knowledge. No knowledge reaches the servant except through one of these three doorways. As for the remaining organs and the outward and inward faculties, it is He who gave them to them and who causes them to grow within them little by little until each person reaches the state appropriate to him. This is so that they may thank God by using these limbs He has given them in obedience to God. Whoever uses them for other than that, they become a proof against him, and he has repaid the blessing with the worst treatment.

Verse 79: "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe." [Note: the verse is about birds being held in the air.]

Ibn Sa'di: That is because they are the ones who benefit from the signs of Allah, those who reflect upon what has been made a sign thereof. As for others, their looking is the looking of heedlessness and amusement. The meaning of the verse in this respect is that Allah Most High created them with a form suited to flying, then subjected to them this subtle air, then deposited in them the strength of movement by which they are able to do so. This is a proof of His wisdom, His vast knowledge, His divine care for all His creation, and the perfection of His power; blessed is the Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verse 89:

{89} When He mentioned earlier that He raises up a witness (shahid) in every nation, He mentioned that here too, and singled out this noble Messenger, saying: ﴿And We have brought you as a witness over these people﴾; that is, over your nation, you bear witness concerning them for good and for evil. This is from the perfection of God's justice, exalted is He: every messenger bears witness over his nation, because he has the greatest knowledge of the deeds of his nation more than anyone else, and he is more just and more compassionate than to bear witness against them except with what they deserve. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness over these people? That Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾. And His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾: in the fundamentals of the religion and its branches, in the rulings of both abodes, and everything that the servants need; it is explained in it with the most complete explanation, with clear expressions and manifest meanings. Indeed, He, exalted is He, repeats in it the great matters that the heart needs to pass over at all times, and He restates them in every hour; He repeats them and displays them with varied expressions and diverse proofs so that they settle in the hearts, and so they bear fruit of good and righteousness according to their firmness in the heart. And indeed, He, exalted is He, gathers in a brief and clear expression many meanings for which the expression serves as a foundation and base. Consider this with the verse that follows this verse, and what it contains of kinds of commands and prohibitions that cannot be counted.

Since this Qur'an is an explanation of all things, it becomes the proof of God over all the servants, so the proof of the wrongdoers is cut off by it, and the Muslims benefit from it, and it becomes guidance (huda) for them, by which they are guided to the matter of their religion and their worldly life, and mercy (rahmah) by which they attain every good in this world and the Hereafter. So guidance is what they attain of beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and mercy is what follows from that of the reward of this world and the Hereafter, such as the soundness and piety of the heart and its tranquility, the completeness of the intellect which is not complete except by being trained upon its meanings, which are the most noble and highest meanings, noble deeds and virtuous character, abundant provision, victory over enemies by word and deed, and attaining the pleasure of God, exalted is He, and His great honor, the enduring bliss of which no one knows what it contains except the Lord, the Merciful.

{90} The justice that God commanded encompasses justice in His right and justice in the rights of His servants. Justice in this regard is the fulfilling of rights completely and in full measure: that the servant discharges what God has made obligatory upon him of rights—financial, bodily, and those combining both—toward God and toward His servants, and deals with creation with complete justice. Every ruler discharges what is upon him within his authority, whether this concerns the supreme office of the Imamate (imamah), the office of judgeship (qada'), or the deputies of the caliph and the deputies of the judge. Justice is what God has enjoined upon them in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger, and commanded them to follow. Among justice in dealings is that you deal with them in contracts of sale, purchase, and all other exchanges by giving in full all that is owed; so you do not diminish their rights, nor cheat them, nor deceive them, nor wrong them. Justice is obligatory, while ihsan (doing good) is a virtue that is recommended. This includes benefiting people with wealth, body, knowledge, and other kinds of benefit, to the extent that it includes kindness to beasts of burden that are eaten and to others. God singled out giving to the near of kin, although it is included in the general command, because of the emphasis on their right, the specific obligation of maintaining ties with them and showing them kindness, and the eagerness for this. This includes all relatives, near and distant, but whoever is nearer has greater claim to kindness. As for His words {and forbids what is shameful}: this is every grave sin that both the sacred laws and natural disposition regard as abominable, such as associating partners with God, killing without right, adultery, theft, self-admiration, arrogance, belittling people, and other abominations. Included under what is reprehensible (munkar) is every sin and act of disobedience connected with the right of God, Exalted, and under oppression (baghy) is every transgression against people in their lives, wealth, and honor. Thus this verse comprehends all commanded and forbidden matters, and nothing remains that is not included in it. This is a principle to which all particular matters return: every matter that involves justice, ihsan, or giving to the near of kin is among what God has commanded, and every matter that involves shameful deeds, what is reprehensible, or oppression is among what God has forbidden. By it the goodness of what God has commanded and the ugliness of what He has forbidden is known, by it the statements of people are evaluated, and to it all conditions return. Blessed is He who placed in His speech guidance, healing, light, and criterion between all things. Therefore He said {He admonishes you}, by it, meaning: by what He has made clear to you in His Book, commanding you with what contains the ultimate good for you and forbidding you from what contains harm for you. {So that you may remember}: what He admonishes you with, so that you understand and comprehend it; for when you remember it and comprehend it, you act according to its requirements, and thus you attain a happiness with no wretchedness in it.

When He commanded what is obligatory in the basic law, He commanded fulfilling what the servant has made obligatory upon himself, and so He said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 98–100:

{98–100} That is: when you intend to recite the Book of Allah, which is the most noble and exalted of books, and in which lie the reform of hearts and many sciences, then Satan is most eager to attack the servant at the beginning of virtuous undertakings, and he strives to divert him from their purposes and meanings. The way to safety from his evil is therefore to seek refuge in Allah and to ask Him for protection from his evil. So the reciter says: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan" (ﷺ), while reflecting on its meaning, relying in his heart upon Allah to turn Satan away from him, striving to repel his whispers and his wicked thoughts, and relying upon the strongest means of repelling him, which is adorning oneself with the adornment of faith and reliance upon Allah (tawakkul). For Satan ﴿has no authority﴾; that is, no domination ﴿over those who believe and upon their Lord﴾, alone with no partner, ﴿who rely upon Him﴾. So Allah repels the evil of Satan from the believers who rely upon Him, and he has no path over them. ﴿His authority is only﴾; that is, his domination ﴿over those who take him as an ally﴾; that is, who make him their protector. This happens when they abandon the guardianship of Allah, enter into obedience to Satan, and join his party. They are the ones who gave him guardianship over themselves, so he incites them to sin with incitement and drives them to the Fire with driving.

{101} Almighty God mentions that those who deny this Qur'an pursue whatever they see as evidence for their position, namely that God, exalted is He, is the Ruler, the Wise, who legislates rulings and replaces one ruling with another, out of His wisdom and mercy. When they see this, they discredit the Messenger and what he brought, and {they say, "You are only a fabricator"}. God, exalted is He, said: {But most of them do not know}. They are ignorant, having no knowledge of their Lord or of His law. And it is well known that the criticism of one who is ignorant, without knowledge, carries no weight, for criticism of a thing is a branch of knowing it and of what it entails of praiseworthiness or blameworthiness.

{102} For this reason God mentioned His wisdom in this, saying: {Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down"}, namely Gabriel, the sanctified Messenger, free from every defect, betrayal and blemish, {with truth}; that is, its descent is with truth, and it contains truth in its reports, its commands and its prohibitions. Therefore there is no way for anyone to discredit it with valid criticism, for when it is known that it is the truth, it is known that whatever opposes and contradicts it is false. {To strengthen those who believe}: at the time of the descent of its verses and their successive arrival upon them, time after time, so that truth continues to reach their hearts little by little, until their faith becomes firmer than the firm mountains. Also, they know that it is the truth, and when He legislates a ruling and then abrogates it, they know that He has replaced it with what is like it or better for them, and that its abrogation is what suits divine wisdom and rational appropriateness. {And as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims}: that is, it guides them to the realities of things, clarifies for them truth from falsehood and guidance from error, and gives them the good news that they have a good reward, abiding in it forever. Also, whenever it descended little by little, it was a greater guidance and good tidings for them than if it had come to them all at once, with thought dispersed over it. Rather, God sends down a ruling, and sometimes more; then when they understand it, comprehend it, know its intended meaning and are satisfied by it, He sends down its like... and so on. For this reason the Companions, may God be pleased with them, attained a great station through it, their characters and natures changed, and they moved to manners, customs and deeds by which they surpassed the first and the last generations. It is more elevated and more fitting for those after them to be educated by its knowledge, to adopt its character, to seek light from its illumination in the darknesses of misguidance and ignorance, and to make it their leader in all circumstances. Through that, their religious and worldly affairs are set right.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 103–105:

{103} He, exalted is He, informs about the statement of the polytheists who denied His Messenger: {They say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."} That is, this Book which he brought is taught to him by a human being, and that human being to whom they point is one whose tongue is non-Arabic (a'jami). {And this} Qur'an {is in a clear Arabic tongue.} Is this claim possible, or does it have any share of plausibility? But the liar lies without reflecting on where his lie will lead, so that his statement contains such contradiction and corruption that it requires its rejection merely by being conceived.

{104} {Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah}, which indicate the clear truth with explicit indication, so they reject them and do not accept them, {Allah will not guide them}, since guidance came to them and they rejected it, so they were punished by being deprived of it and by Allah's forsaking them. {And for them} in the Hereafter {is a painful punishment.}

{105} {Only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah fabricate falsehood}; that is, the fabrication of lies only issues from {those who do not believe in the signs of Allah}, like those who obstinately oppose His Messenger {after the clear proofs had come to them}. {And it is those who are the liars}; that is, lying is confined to them, and they are more deserving of the label than anyone else. As for Muhammad (ﷺ), who believes in the signs of Allah and submits to his Lord, it is impossible that he would lie about Allah or invent against Him what He did not say. His enemies accused him of the lie that is in fact their own attribute, so Allah exposed their disgrace and made their scandals manifest; to Him, exalted is He, belongs all praise.

{114} He commands His servants to eat of what Allah has provided them of animals, grains, fruits and other things. {Lawful and good}; that is, in a state of possessing these two qualities: it must not be something Allah has forbidden, nor the product of usurpation (ghasb) or the like. {124} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿The Sabbath was only prescribed﴾, that is, as an obligation, ﴿for those who differed concerning it﴾, when they went astray from the day of Friday. They were the Jews, and their disagreement became the cause for it to be obligatory upon them to honor and glorify the Sabbath. Otherwise, the true excellence belongs to Friday, the day to which Allah guided this Ummah. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, so He will make clear to them the one who is in the right from the one who is in falsehood, and the one who deserves reward from the one who deserves punishment.

{125} That is: let your calling (of people) to the path of your Lord, the Straight Path which comprises beneficial knowledge and righteous action, be directed to all creatures, whether Muslim or disbelieving, {with wisdom}; that is, to each person according to his condition, understanding, acceptance and submission. Among wisdom is calling with knowledge and not with ignorance, beginning with what is most important and then what is next in importance, with what is closest to minds and understanding, with what will be most fully accepted, and with gentleness and softness. If he submits through wisdom, well and good; otherwise, one moves on with him to calling by good admonition (al-maw'izah al-hasanah), which is command and prohibition accompanied by encouragement and warning: either by mentioning the benefits contained in the commands and enumerating them, and the harms in the prohibitions and enumerating them; or by mentioning the honour of those who uphold the religion of God and the humiliation of those who do not; or by mentioning what God has prepared for the obedient of reward both in this world and the next, and what He has prepared for the disobedient of punishment both in this world and the next. If the one being called believes that what he holds is the truth, or if he is a caller to falsehood, then he is to be argued with in the best manner (bi-allati hiya ahsan), which means the methods most likely to win his acceptance, rationally and by transmitted evidence. Among this is arguing against him with the proofs which he himself believes in, for that is closer to achieving the aim. The argument should not lead to quarrelling or abuse which would defeat its purpose and prevent any benefit from it; rather, its intent should be guiding creatures to the truth, not mere victory over the opponent or the like. As for His saying: {Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way}: He knows the cause which led him to straying, He knows his deeds that follow from his misguidance, and He will recompense him for them. {And He is most knowing of the guided}: He knows that they are fit for guidance, so He guided them; then He bestowed His favour upon them and chose them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 16, verses 126–128:

{126} The Exalted says, permitting justice and urging virtue and goodness: ﴿And if you punish﴾ whoever has wronged you by word or deed, ﴿then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾, without exceeding what was inflicted upon you. ﴿But if you are patient﴾ and refrain from retaliation and pardon their offence, ﴿it is better for the patient﴾ than exacting retribution. What is with Allah is better for you and better in its outcome, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah﴾.

{127–128} Then He commanded His Messenger to be patient in calling the creation to Allah, to seek Allah's help in that, and not to rely upon himself, so He said: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾, meaning it is He who helps you to it and makes you firm. ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ if you call them and see no acceptance of your call from them, for grief does not benefit you in anything. ﴿And do not be in distress﴾, i.e., in hardship and constriction, ﴿over what they plot﴾, for their plotting returns upon them, while you are among the God-fearing and the doers of good, and Allah is with the God-fearing and the doers of good, by His help, His success and His support. They are the ones who guard themselves against disbelief and sins and excel in the worship of Allah, by worshipping Allah as though they see Him; and if they do not see Him, then He sees them. And goodness toward the creation is by bestowing benefit upon them in every way. We ask Allah to make us among the God-fearing and the doers of good.

The commentary on Surah an-Nahl is complete. And to Allah belongs all praise and favour.
